sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion and has grown only 4.9% in FY2025 to $51.8 billion [F8][D274][F10][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue and contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% growth, while natural gas added 4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D551][D342][D553][D586][D585].
The U.S. was 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of growth, with non-U.S. adding 2.0pp [D382][D384][D400].
FY2025 sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 while revenue rose 4.9%, so profit grew slower than revenue [D343][D342].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025, faster than the 4.9% revenue growth [D352][D342].
Net margin of 15.4% in FY2025 sat below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].

FY2025 earnings fell on lower commodity prices, partly offset by Marathon Oil operations, with higher DD&A of $1.3 billion and production and operating expenses of $875 million from the acquisition [P6][P17].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% in FY2025 from 32.4% in FY2024, and net margin of 15.4% was 3.3pp lower than the prior year [D332][D298][F30][D351].
Net interest expense increased in FY2025 on debt assumed from the Marathon Oil acquisition [P10].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median [F59][F20][D333][D855].
Operating cash flow fell 1.6% in FY2025 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [D346][P6].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, and capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 [D833][D834][D222].
Stock-based compensation was 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D334].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025 against $6.5 billion of cash, and the current ratio was 1.30x versus a 1.45x window median [D335][F113][F153][D843].
Net cash is only reported through FY2020, when it was net debt of $12.9 billion, or -67.0% of revenue, because long-term debt is not tagged after that year [D155][D156][F157].
FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capital spending, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks and dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, and the diluted share count rose 6.1% in FY2025 [P31][D356].
Revenue in the table is a later recast for every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10][R1].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix recast and first-reported years are not like-for-like, so the trend above should be read with that caveat [R1].
Long-term debt is not tagged after FY2020, so net cash and the net-cash peer rank cannot be computed for FY2025 [F157][R6].
Leverage after the Marathon Oil acquisition is therefore unmeasured here, which limits any balance-sheet verdict [R6].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023, the only decline in the last four years [F8][D274][R2].
That drop was price-led rather than volume-led, so it reads as cyclical exposure rather than a structural break [R2].
Whether FY2026 net margin holds above the 17.9% window median or falls toward the 15.4% FY2025 level, in the FY2026 10-K [D831][F30].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the 2.07x net-income median or slips toward the 1.52x window low, in the FY2026 10-K [D855][D854].
Whether the diluted share count reverses its 6.1% FY2025 increase or buybacks resume shrinking it, in the FY2026 10-K [D356].
